QuestionStmt.S: 4 red balls and 5 green balls are selected from $n$ balls. If the sum of both the selections is greater than ${}^{n+1}C_4$ then the value of $n$ is equal to

Solution.S:
4 red balls can be selected from $n$ balls in ${}^nC_4$ ways.

5 green balls can be selected from $n$ balls in ${}^nC_5$ ways.

Sum of both selections is greater than ${}^{n+1}C_4$:

$${}^nC_4 + {}^nC_5 > {}^{n+1}C_4$$

$$\Rightarrow \frac{n!}{4!(n-4)!} + \frac{n!}{5!(n-5)!} > \frac{(n+1)!}{4!(n-3)!}$$

$$\Rightarrow \frac{n!}{4!(n-5)!} \left[ \frac{1}{n-4} + \frac{1}{5} \right] > \frac{(n+1)n!}{4!(n-3)(n-4)(n-5)!}$$

$$\Rightarrow \frac{5 + n - 4}{5(n-4)} > \frac{n+1}{(n-3)(n-4)}$$

$$\Rightarrow \frac{n+1}{5} > \frac{n+1}{n-3} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{5} > \frac{1}{n-3} \Rightarrow n-3 > 5 \Rightarrow n > 8$$

Thus the correct option is A: $n > 8$.
